headline: Mandatory Registration for Remote Northern Yukon Backcountry
reservation: Accessing this fly-in wilderness requires mandatory registration with Parks Canada via the Old Crow office or Inuvik office. While there are no formal campgrounds, users must distinguish between park entry registration and the logistical coordination needed for air charter landing authorizations. Reservation systems for local services change seasonally; consult the Parks Canada site and the Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation for current protocols and cultural land use permissions.

days.title: Old Crow Flats and Wetlands

stops.name: Old Crow River
stops.detail: Traverse the winding waterway that serves as the lifeblood of the park, offering views of the vast wetland plateau.

stops.name: Crow Flats
stops.detail: Observe the Van Tat (Crow Flats) area, a significant wetland complex vital for migratory birds and the Porcupine Caribou Herd.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for air charter or river boat transfer; conditions vary.
days.note: Travel is dependent on water levels and local guide availability.

days.title: Arctic Mountains and Plateaus

stops.name: Thomas Creek
stops.detail: Explore the archaeological significance of the region where ancient history and northern tundra ecosystems meet.

stops.name: British Mountains Footprints
stops.detail: Identify the rolling transitions between the wetlands and the stark northern mountain ranges.

days.driving: Allow all day for trekking; conditions vary by terrain.
days.note: Zero marked trails; navigation skills are essential for this remote region.

days.title: Gwitchin Heritage and River Vistas

stops.name: John Tizya Centre
stops.detail: Return to Old Crow to understand the Vuntut Gwitchin cultural connection to the landscape.

stops.name: Porcupine River Confluence
stops.detail: View the convergence of the Porcupine and Old Crow rivers, a historic hub for northern travel.

days.driving: Allow 2-4 hours for return river travel; conditions vary.
days.note: Plan departure around flight schedules out of Old Crow.

intel.title: No Road Access
intel.text: Vuntut is only accessible by air or water; there are no roads leading into the park from the Yukon highway system. Most visitors charter flights from Inuvik or Old Crow.

intel.title: Old Crow Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are extremely limited and must be sourced in Old Crow before entering the park. Availability fluctuates, so verify local stocks before arrival.

intel.title: Satellite Communication Only
intel.text: There is no cellular service or internet within the park boundaries. Visitors must carry reliable satellite communication devices for emergencies.

intel.title: Midnight Sun Window
intel.text: Summer visits benefit from 24-hour daylight, but weather can change rapidly with snow possible in any month. High water in June may impact river travel.

intel.title: Airport Staging
intel.text: Standard vehicle parking is not applicable here; staging occurs at the Old Crow or Inuvik air terminals. Coordinate gear storage with your charter provider.

plan.arrival: Inuvik flight arrival, transfer to local charter for Old Crow, and mandatory check-in at the Parks Canada office.
plan.vehicle: No road vehicles; travel is via air charter or non-motorized/motorized boat depending on the season.
plan.goldenHour: Midnight Sun views from any high ridge overlooking the Old Crow Flats.
